name: FastBinarySearch
workload: Scalar and vectorial (SSE-4/AVX-2) insertion-point search for random query points in a sorted array of 2048 single- or double-precision floats
claimed_speedup: up to two orders of magnitude (100x) throughput vs classic binary search (paper abstract); README benchmark on gcc 7 libstdc++: DirectCacheFMA scalar 496.44 M searches/s vs LowerBound (std::lower_bound) scalar 14.02 M searches/s, single precision (~35x, derived from page data); AVX-2 DirectFMA 992.87 M searches/s vs LowerBound scalar 14.02 M searches/s (~71x, derived from page data)
compiler_and_flags: gcc 7 (exact optimization flags not stated in README)
stars_or_usage: 153 stars; subset shipped in NAG Library routine m01ndc
tradeoffs: Best suited to roughly log-uniform/logarithmically distributed sorted float arrays; the O(1) indexed variant needs extra memory and upfront preprocessing of the array; header-only C++ API differs from std::lower_bound's iterator-based signature; largest gains require SSE/AVX vectorial batch queries, scalar-only gains are smaller
caveats: Benchmark CPU (Xeon E5-2620 v3, Haswell-era 2014) and gcc 7 are dated; exact compiler flags not published in the README, so tier is capped at B; peer-reviewed JPDC 2018 paper predates the current README table but numbers match; the largest reported ratios compare vectorial (batch, AVX-2) throughput against LowerBound's scalar-only figure, which is an apples-to-oranges comparison unless the caller is doing batched queries
found_via: arXiv search 'branchless or SIMD binary search faster than std::lower_bound' -> arXiv:1506.08620 (Cannizzo, "Fast and Vectorizable Alternative to Binary Search in O(1) Applicable to a Wide Domain of Sorted Arrays of Floating Point Numbers", J. Parallel Distrib. Comput. 113:37-50, 2018); cross-verified via github.com/fabiocannizzo/FastBinarySearch README and GitHub API metadata
